source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"At least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week, with no need for regular activity on most other days.","B":"At least 30 minutes of light physical activity each day, with muscle- and bone-strengthening activity avoided until adulthood.","C":"At least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity daily, including aerobic and age-appropriate strengthening activities.","D":"The same 150-minutes-per-week target used for adults, because children and adolescents do not have a separate activity guideline today."}}
source_row.rationale: The CDC recommends that children and adolescents (ages 6-17) engage in at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity daily, including a variety of aerobic, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activities throughout the week, to support healthy growth, development, and long-term health.
source_row.source_detail: CDC child activity guideline: ages 6–17 need ≥60 min/day moderate-to-vigorous activity; vigorous and muscle-strengthening activity at least 3 days/week, with bone-strengthening activity also 3 days/week. CDC page updated 2025-12-04; reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
